title: THROW Statement
description: Learn how to raise exceptions and rethrow caught errors using the THROW statement.

data.text: The THROW statement raises an exception and transfers execution to a CATCH block of a TRY...CATCH construct. It is the recommended replacement for RAISERROR.

data.title: THROW with parameters
data.content: Raises a custom error with error number, message, and state.

data.title: THROW to rethrow caught error
data.content: Rethrows the error caught in the CATCH block.
data.code:
BEGIN TRY
    -- statements that may cause errors
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    THROW;
END CATCH

data.title: THROW Key Points
points: THROW is the modern replacement for RAISERROR.
Use THROW without arguments in a CATCH block to rethrow the caught error.
Error numbers must be between 50,000 and 2,147,483,647.
THROW does not support printf-style message formatting.
